title: audit current US_STATES
question_answered: Entry count, distinct canonical values, and structural defects (missing self-maps, empty values, overlaps, country scoping) of US_STATES as it exists today. Source lines quoted; no changes proposed to the dictionary.
source: _upstream/src/normalize.py lines 216-229 (literal), 250-254 (self-map loop), 318/331-335 (matcher). Read-only: file text exec'd in memory with polars stubbed; no import, no __pycache__ written; no raw TSV opened.
headline: US_STATES is structurally perfect: 52 literal entries, 52 distinct canonical values, zero duplicate/empty/malformed entries, all 50 states + dc + pr present, and all 52 self-maps present at runtime (104 entries). The missing-self-map defect is FR_REGIONS-only. Every real defect is in the MATCHING rule at normalize.py:333 (whole-component exact match), not in the dictionary contents. The worst is NEW: a city component equal to a single-word state name is consumed as the state AND deleted from the token stream, and can make a wrong state appear.

entry_count.extraction_method: exec of file text truncated immediately before 'STATE_MAPS = {' to capture the pre-loop literal

coverage.arithmetic: 50 reference codes - 0 missing = 50 present; set difference = [dc, pr]

key_shape.multi_word_note: These can never appear as a single addr_tokens entry because build_profile.py:28 defines TOKEN_RE = [a-z0-9]+. Their absence from addr_tokens is a tokenisation artifact, not a data gap.

self_maps.loop_source: normalize.py:252-254  for _m in (US_STATES, IN_STATES): for _v in list(_m.values()): _m.setdefault(_v, _v)
self_maps.conclusion: The known missing-self-map defect applies to FR_REGIONS only. US_STATES self-maps are complete.

overlaps_and_scoping.country_scoping: STATE_MAPS is country-keyed at normalize.py:318 (smap = STATE_MAPS.get(country, {})). US_STATES is unreachable from France or India rows. SOUND - do not change.
overlaps_and_scoping.name_canon_verdict: not a defect - NAME_CANON applies to business names (normalize.py:281), ADDR_CANON_COMMON to addresses (normalize.py:347); they never meet

structural_defects.name: whole-component exact match loses the state when a ZIP shares the component
structural_defects.evidence: normalize.py:333 `if ck in smap` tests the ENTIRE component only
structural_defects.exposure_metric: by_country[US].dig5 / rows (OCCURRENCES per row, not a row fraction)
structural_defects.row_level_impact: GAP - not measurable; addr_tokens discards component boundaries. build_profile.py:115 makes dig5 an occurrence count, so the affected row share is <= 0.1098 and unknown.

structural_defects.name: bare-word components consumed as states and DELETED from the token stream
structural_defects.confidence: CONFIRMED behaviour, LIKELY as a real-data problem
structural_defects.mechanism: the matched component is `continue`d at normalize.py:335 so its tokens are never emitted; city_comps is emptied too
structural_defects.row_level_impact: GAP - token occurrences are not misfire counts

structural_defects.name: ADDR_CANON_COMMON hijacks the wy state code (wy -> way)
structural_defects.absent_note: wy absent in test_s3 means count <= floor 274, NOT zero

structural_defects.name: NEW: a city component equal to a single-word state name is eaten, producing a WRONG state
structural_defects.confidence: CONFIRMED behaviour, LIKELY real-data problem; row count is a GAP
structural_defects.mechanism: 40 of the 52 keys are single-word state names, many of which are common US city names; the component is matched and then `continue`d, so the city token is deleted from toks AND city_comps

errors: true state ga not captured because of defect A

structural_defects.headline_claim: Appending one ZIP to a Georgia address flips the resolved state from ga to wa and destroys the city field. A postcode can change the resolved state to a different, WRONG one - strictly worse than a missing state.
structural_defects.row_level_impact: GAP - build_profile.py:126-127 discards component boundaries, so a 'washington' occurrence may be the state, the city, or a street name. Deliberately not converted to a row count.

structural_defects.name: NEW: no break - the LAST matching component wins, so the result is position-dependent
structural_defects.mechanism: normalize.py:334 assigns state = smap[ck] on every match with no break, so a later match silently overwrites an earlier one
structural_defects.note: Last-wins is defensible under a canonical convention but is currently coincidental, not enforced. Reordering two components flips the resolved state.

structural_defects.name: NEW: punctuated D.C. yields a confidently WRONG state instead of an empty one
structural_defects.mechanism: the ck cleaner turns 'D.C.' into 'd c', which is not a key, so the real state is lost - but the preceding component 'Washington' still matches and emits wa
structural_defects.generalisation: When a real state component fails to match, defect D converts the failure from an empty state into a wrong state.

vocabulary_exposure.absent_means: count <= top-4000 floor, NOT zero occurrences (build_profile.py:27 TOPN=4000, prune() lines 45-49 drops count<=1 every 8 chunks)
vocabulary_exposure.correction_to_prior_draft: A pre-existing draft of D074 claimed '45 of 52' code tokens present for all three test splits. Recount gives 45/45/38; test_s3 has 14 absent codes, not 7. Its test_s3 occurrence figure (154358) was correct, so the error was in the type count only.

penn.note: standard PA abbreviation; surrounding component not recoverable from the profile

del_resolves.reason: 'del' is already the Delaware code in US_STATES

france_relevance.note: The France-side analogue of defect B, flagged because France is the scored country. FR_REGIONS conclusions belong to D070/D073; this task only establishes the mechanism.

mechanism_demo.note: FR_REGIONS maps paris->idf, so a standalone Paris component is consumed and the city token deleted

france_relevance.why_not: a 'paris' token occurrence is not proof of a standalone Paris component; addr_tokens discards component boundaries

recommendations.action: Do NOT add states to US_STATES - 50/50 + dc + pr present and clean; the dictionary is not the bottleneck
Only dictionary change worth considering: penn -> pa (163/467/497 occurrences). No action on the five missing territories - absent from every test split
Fix defect D first - require a state match to be the final component or be followed only by a postcode, so a city named after a state cannot yield a wrong state or be deleted
Fix defect A - after the whole-component test fails, also try a trailing '<code|name> <5-digit>' pattern
Make last-wins explicit (defect E) by breaking on the first positional match or asserting the matched component is last
Fix the wy -> way collision (defect C) in ADDR_CANON_COMMON
Explicitly NOT recommended: touching US_STATES self-maps (already 52/52 at runtime) or mirroring US_STATES onto FR_REGIONS (owned by D070, zero measured effect per the work order)

gaps: Row-level misfire counts for defects A, B, D and E: build_profile.py:126-127 splits on [,;] and pushes [a-z0-9]+ matches into one flat Counter, discarding component boundaries. The profile cannot distinguish a standalone state component from a word inside a longer component. Not estimated.
dig5/dig6 are occurrence totals (build_profile.py:115), not row counts, so the affected row share for defect A is bounded above by dig5/rows but unavailable exactly.
The 12 multi-word state names are structurally invisible to addr_tokens and cannot be validated.
'Absent' from top-4000 never means zero occurrences, so no rate was computed from an absent token.

Whether French or Indian addresses contain a component matching a US_STATES key was not tested at component level; the inference that they cannot match rests on the country-keyed lookup, not on measurement.
features.py / keys.py were not examined, so whether any of these defects change the final submission is unproven.
